title: [CQ-V10a] Pure architecture rule engine
description:
Objective: the pure, IO-free core of CQ-V10 (changed-code architecture rules). It parses versioned project import rules, extracts imports from changed source text, surfaces dynamic uncertainty, and evaluates forbidden edges for only the rules the changed code selects. Split out of CQ-V10 (task-db328cda) by architect-4ae016fb on 2026-10-29 as a size split: V10 owns the candidate and CLI wiring and plans against these exact names.

Interface, a new module packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts, importing only util/errors.js and util/affectedFiles.js:
- `export interface ArchitectureRule { readonly id: string; readonly from: readonly string[]; readonly forbid: readonly string[]; readonly reason: string }`.
- `export interface ArchitectureRules { readonly version: 1; readonly rules: readonly ArchitectureRule[] }`.
- `export function parseArchitectureRules(text: string): ArchitectureRules`. It throws invalidInput, naming the field, unless all of these hold:
  - the JSON has exactly the keys {version, rules} and version is 1;
  - there are 1-100 rules, each with exactly the keys {id, from, forbid, reason};
  - ids are unique and match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$;
  - from and forbid are non-empty lists of at most 32 normalized repo-relative path prefixes (normalizeAffectedFile(p) === p);
  - reason is 1-300 characters.
- `export interface ImportRef { readonly line: number; readonly specifier: string }`.
- `export interface ImportUncertainty { readonly line: number; readonly reason: 'dynamic-import' | 'non-literal-require' | 'unresolved-relative' }`.
- `export function extractImports(text: string): { imports: ImportRef[]; uncertain: ImportUncertainty[] }`.
  - It finds string-literal specifiers of: `import ... from`, side-effect `import`, `export ... from`, `import()` and `require()`, including type-only imports.
  - A non-literal `import(expr)` gives 'dynamic-import', and a non-literal `require(expr)` gives 'non-literal-require'. Neither is ever dropped.
  - Comments and string contents are not scanned as code.
  - Line numbers are 1-based.
- `export function resolveImport(fromPath: string, specifier: string, treePaths: ReadonlySet<string>): string | null`.
  - Relative specifiers only. A '.js' specifier maps to '.ts', '.tsx', '.js' or '.mjs' in that order, and a directory resolves to its '/index' file.
  - A bare package specifier gives null (external).
  - A relative specifier that matches nothing gives null; the evaluator reports it as 'unresolved-relative'.
- `export interface ArchitectureFinding { readonly ruleId: string; readonly file: string; readonly line: number; readonly specifier: string; readonly resolved: string }`.
- `export interface ArchitectureResult { readonly outcome: 'passed' | 'failed' | 'inconclusive'; readonly selectedRules: readonly string[]; readonly violations: readonly ArchitectureFinding[]; readonly uncertain: readonly (ImportUncertainty & { readonly file: string })[] }`.
- `export function evaluateArchitecture(rules: ArchitectureRules, changed: readonly { path: string; text: string }[], treePaths: ReadonlySet<string>): ArchitectureResult`.
  - A rule is selected iff one of its `from` prefixes covers at least one changed path. Coverage compares whole segments: equal to the prefix, or starting with it plus '/'.
  - Only changed .ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs and .cjs files covered by a selected rule are scanned.
  - A resolved import covered by that rule's `forbid` is a violation.
  - Every uncertainty in a scanned file is surfaced.
  - Outcome precedence: any violation gives failed; else any uncertainty gives inconclusive; else passed.
  - Output is sorted deterministically.

Scope boundaries: this module and its unit tests only. No Git, no IO, no CLI, no store or schema change. Never directly edit .moe.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: parseArchitectureRules accepts the documented shape and refuses each malformed variant (wrong version, extra keys, duplicate or invalid ids, empty or non-normalized prefixes, over-limit lists, bad reason) with INVALID_INPUT naming the field, one test per variant.

extractImports finds every static, side-effect, re-export, type-only, literal dynamic-import and literal require specifier with its line. It reports non-literal import() and require() as uncertainty, never dropped, and ignores comments and string contents.

evaluateArchitecture selects only rules whose from covers a changed path. It reports forbidden resolved imports as violations with rule, file and line, surfaces unresolved-relative and dynamic uncertainty, and applies the precedence failed > inconclusive > passed, with deterministic ordering.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS + IMPLEMENTATION: types and parseArchitectureRules. Load test-driven-development: write the test rows first, see them fail, then implement.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts.
- Header comment: pure and IO-free, the engine of CQ-V10, which (task-db328cda) consumes these exact names.
- Import ONLY `invalidInput` from '../util/errors.js' and `normalizeAffectedFile` from '../util/affectedFiles.js'. No node: builtins and no other module.
- Export the six interfaces exactly as the task description spells them: ArchitectureRule, ArchitectureRules, ImportRef, ImportUncertainty, ArchitectureFinding and ArchitectureResult.
- Keep the module lean (about 350 lines when the task is done).

`parseArchitectureRules(text)`. Error handling: every refusal is `invalidInput(field, reason)`, with explicit error handling for each field. Field names follow the validateRequiredChecks idiom in state/validators.ts:
1. A non-string text, or a JSON.parse failure, gives field `architectureRules`. Catch the SyntaxError; never let it escape raw.
2. A root that is not a non-null, non-array object gives `architectureRules`.
3. Each own key outside {version, rules} gives field `<key>`, reason 'is not a supported architecture rules field'. Unknown keys are checked before missing ones.
4. version must be the number 1, compared strictly with ===. '1', 2 and a missing version are refused: `version`.
5. rules must be an array of 1-100 entries: `rules`.
6. Per rule i:
   - a non-null, non-array object: `rules[i]`;
   - keys outside {id, from, forbid, reason}: `rules[i].<key>`;
   - id a string matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$: `rules[i].id`;
   - ids unique: the later duplicate's `rules[i].id`, reason 'must be unique'.
7. from and forbid are arrays of 1-32 entries: `rules[i].from` or `rules[i].forbid`.
   - Each entry j goes through normalizeAffectedFile(entry, 'rules[i].from[j]'). It already throws invalidInput naming that field for non-strings and for empty, absolute, drive-letter and '..' paths.
   - Then `entry !== normalized` throws invalidInput('rules[i].from[j]', 'must be normalized: <normalized>'). This is the validateCheckPaths idiom.
8. reason is a string of 1-300 UTF-16 code units (.length): `rules[i].reason`.

Return a FRESH `{ version: 1, rules }`. Rebuild each rule as `{ id, from: [...], forbid: [...] , reason }`, keeping input order and that key order. Never return the parsed object itself.

Create packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.test.ts (vitest) with `describe('parseArchitectureRules')`. Build documents with JSON.stringify, so escaping cannot hide a mistake.
- P1: a two-rule document is toStrictEqual the canonical object, and Object.keys of a rule is exactly ['id','from','forbid','reason'].
- P2: exact limits are accepted: 100 rules, 32 prefixes in both lists, a 300-unit reason and a 64-character id.
- P3: one `it.each` row per refused variant, so each variant is its own test.
  - Each row asserts toMatchObject({ code: MoeErrorCode.INVALID_INPUT, codeName: 'INVALID_INPUT', context: { field } }) with the EXACT field, never a bare toThrow().
  - Rows giving architectureRules: invalid JSON; a root array; a root null.
  - Rows giving version: version 2; version '1'; version missing.
  - An extra top-level key gives that key's name.
  - Rows giving rules: rules missing; not an array; []; 101 entries.
  - A non-object rule gives rules[0]. An extra rule key gives rules[0].<key>.
  - Rows giving rules[0].id: id missing; uppercase; leading '-'; 65 characters. A duplicate id gives rules[1].id.
  - Rows giving rules[0].from: from missing; []; 33 entries.
  - Rows giving rules[0].forbid: forbid []; 33 entries.
  - Rows giving rules[0].from[0]: 'src/state/'; './src'; a backslash-separated prefix; 'src//state'; ' src'; '../x'; '/abs'; 'C:/x'; ''; a number.
  - A bad forbid entry at index 1 gives rules[0].forbid[1].
  - Rows giving rules[0].reason: reason missing; ''; 301 units; a non-string.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS + IMPLEMENTATION: extractImports(text), in the two files created in step 1: architectureRules.ts and architectureRules.test.ts. Report both in modifiedFiles.

Build it as ONE linear pass that lexes significant tokens, followed by a token-pattern pass. Use no regex over the raw text other than single-character tests, and no parser dependency.

LEXER (code mode):
- Line numbers are 1-based. LF, CR, CRLF (counted once), U+2028 and U+2029 each end a line. Test for line terminators BEFORE generic whitespace, because the \s class also matches U+2028/2029. These are JS line terminators, so a `//` comment ends at ANY of them; otherwise a comment containing U+2028 would hide a live require after it.
- Skip whitespace, including the BOM. A `#!` at offset 0 starts a comment line. `//` comments run to the line end, and `/* */` comments count the lines inside them.
- Quoted strings ('...' and the double-quote form) honour backslash escapes, including backslash plus a line terminator (continuation). As recovery, an unescaped LF or CR also ends the string, so an unterminated string never swallows later lines.
  - The token value is the COOKED string. Decode backslash n r t b f v 0, backslash-x plus 2 hex digits, backslash-u plus 4 hex digits, and backslash-u{hex}. A continuation decodes to nothing, and any other backslash-c decodes to c. A hex-escaped '../tools/t.js' is therefore still '../tools/t.js'.
- Backtick templates: the text honours escapes. `${` enters code mode with a pushed brace-depth counter, so nested braces and nested templates work, and a `}` at depth 0 resumes the text.
  - A template with no `${` is ONE literal token holding its cooked value.
  - A template with substitutions is one NON-literal token. Its substitution tokens follow and are scanned like any code.
- Identifiers start with [A-Za-z$_] or a backslash-u escape, and continue with [A-Za-z0-9$_] or backslash-u escapes. Any non-ASCII character that is not whitespace or a line terminator also counts as an identifier character.
  - Escapes are decoded into the name, so a backslash-u0072 'equire' IS require.
  - Each identifier token records `member`: the previous token was `.` or `#`, as in a property or private name.
- Numbers: a digit, or a `.` followed by a digit, then [0-9A-Za-z_.]*.
- Punctuators: `...` is one token. Every other punctuator is a single character, so `?.` is `?` followed by `.`.
- A `/` that does not start `//` or `/*` begins a REGEX only when the previous token is:
  - none;
  - a punctuator other than `)` and `]` (`${` counts as `{`);
  - or a non-member keyword among: return typeof instanceof in of new delete void throw case do else yield await.
  Otherwise it is division, and division also follows a completed template.
  - The regex body honours backslash escapes and [...] classes, where `/` does not end the body. It ends at `/` plus [A-Za-z]* flags.
  - If a line terminator or EOF comes first, the `/` is emitted as a punctuator and lexing resumes right after it. This line-local recovery bounds a misread.
- Unterminated comments, templates and regexes end at EOF. extractImports NEVER throws on any string input.

RECOGNIZER (tokens in source order):
- An `import`, `export` or `require` identifier with member=true is ignored: obj.import(...), x?.require(...), this.#require. A spread `...` is not `.`.
- `import (`:
  - If the next token is a literal (a quoted string, or a template with no substitutions) and the token after it is `)` or `,` (the comma allows import attributes), it is an ImportRef.
  - Otherwise it is an uncertainty {line: the import token's line, reason 'dynamic-import'}.
- `import .` (import.meta) is ignored. `import` followed by a quoted string is a side-effect ImportRef.
- Every other `import`, and every `export`, runs a CLAUSE SCAN from the next token.
  - The scan continues while each token is an identifier other than import or export, a quoted string, or one of `{ } , *`.
  - When the identifier `from` is immediately followed by a quoted string, that string is an ImportRef and the scan ends. Any other token ends the scan with nothing.
  - This covers default, named, namespace, `type`, inline `type` and string-named bindings, `export *`, `export * as ns`, `export {a} from` and `export type {T} from`.
  - `export const`, `export default` and TS `import x = require(...)` stop at their first other token; the require rule handles the last one.
  - The main loop still visits every token. Because the scan stops at import and export, the pass stays linear.
- `require (`: a literal followed by `)` is an ImportRef. Otherwise it is an uncertainty {line: the require token's line, 'non-literal-require'}. A `require` that is not called (require.resolve, typeof require) is ignored.
- An ImportRef's line is the line of its specifier literal, so a multi-line named import reports the line of its `from` string.
- False-positive uncertainty is the accepted direction. A method NAMED import or require reads as a non-literal call. A missed import is never acceptable.

TESTS, `describe('extractImports')`. Each test asserts the exact {imports, uncertain} with toStrictEqual, lines included:
- X1 static forms: default; named; namespace; `a, { b }`; multi-line named; `import type {T}`; `import { type T, U }`; a side-effect import; `export * from`; `export * as ns from`; `export { a as b } from`; `export type { T } from`; both quote styles.
- X2 literal dynamic forms: `await import('./a.js')`; a no-substitution template import; `import('./d.json', { with: { type: 'json' } })`; `require('./r')`; a no-substitution template require; the TS type position `let t: import('./types.js').T`.
- X3 uncertainty: `import(name)`, `import('./a' + b)`, a template import with a ${} substitution, `require(dep)` and `require('./a' + b)`. Each gives an uncertainty with its exact line and reason, and NO import. A literal require inside a ${} substitution is still an ImportRef.
- X4 nothing found:
  - `//` comments, and a multi-line `/* */` comment (later lines keep correct numbers);
  - a JSDoc {import('./doc.js').T};
  - import text inside quoted strings and inside template text;
  - the regex literal /import x from 'y'/;
  - obj.import('./m') and obj.require('./m');
  - import.meta.url and require.resolve('./r');
  - { import: 1, require: 2 }.
- X5 lexing traps:
  - the regex /[']/ followed by an import on the same line: found;
  - `a / b / c` then a require on the same line: found;
  - f(...require('./spread')): found;
  - a backslash-u escaped require: found;
  - a hex-escaped specifier: reported cooked;
  - U+2028 ending a `//` comment, then a require: found, on line 2;
  - CRLF input: correct lines;
  - an unterminated string, then an import on the next line: found;
  - a `#!` first line;
  - '' gives { imports: [], uncertain: [] }.

QA advisory 2, verified with a tsx probe on HEAD 7f04b869:
- The module follows the plan's candidate order literally, so './', '../x/' and 'x/.' try joined+ext before joined/index. Node treats '.', '..', a trailing '/' and a trailing '/.' as directory-only.
- With a decoy sibling, tree {src/state.ts, src/state/index.ts} and one rule (from src/ui, forbid src/state), `import x from '../state/'` resolves to src/state.ts and the result is 'passed'. Without the decoy it is 'failed'.
- Extensionless '../state' choosing the file first matches Node's CJS resolution, so that case is fine.
- Not fixed here: QA marked it optional, and pending waiver prop-7401cd0b freezes these bytes. Filed as bug task-54dc3d385ef542a08a0a8e9aa2ce8969 (BACKLOG, dependsOn this task).

Gotcha: the M5 and M9 vitest logs contain NUL bytes (the octal test's diff output), so GNU grep treated them as binary and silently printed nothing. Use `grep -a`.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. I read the module in full as an attacker. No byte changes.

1. Hiding an import:
   - Checked and holding: every JS line terminator ends `//` (M1); escaped identifiers and specifiers are cooked (M5, M9); `...` is not `.`; code inside ${} is scanned; a recognized regex body is opaque; CRLF works; .d.ts files are scanned.
   - NEW real finding. The plan's "line-local recovery" premise is false for template and `/* */` state. Six probes on HEAD hide a require on a LATER line with uncertain=[]; in node vm, three of them run the require.
     - Triggers: a division misread as a regex after `}`, `!` or ++, followed by a path template; a regex read as division after `extends` or `export default`; a CJS `<!--` comment; a backtick in TSX text.
     - Filed as task-16628bef427b426aa9d8fc6ac1d19534 (HIGH). The fix is a design decision, because the contract forbids new uncertainty reasons, and these bytes are frozen under the waiver.
   - QA's advisory 2 is a decoy-file bypass, filed as task-54dc3d385ef542a08a0a8e9aa2ce8969.
   - V10 was told in comment-6ae9a36d, and #governors in msg-745ef199.
2. Pathological input: holding.
   - No recursion. Clause scans are disjoint. Escape runs are bounded (\u{ up to 0x10ffff, octal up to 3 digits). regexOffUntil keeps failed regex scans linear (M10).
   - All X6 rows pass. No backtracking regex runs over raw text.
3. Empty inputs: holding. '' gives none. No changed files gives passed. An empty tree gives inconclusive.
4. Determinism: holding. Sorts are by code unit with full tie-breaks, the key order is fixed, and Set/Map are used only for has/get. Identical duplicate findings are possible and harmless.
5. Purity: holding. Exactly the 2 util imports; no node:; no module-level let/var; the shared sentinels are never mutated.
6. Rails: holding. Forbidden-token grep exit 1 (none found). No .moe edits, no Git writes, verified-local untouched.

A non-string text on a scanned entry throws TypeError. That is the caller's contract and theoretical here.

Residuals:
- JSX text is lexed as code, and that is not line-local for backticks.
- A regex after a non-control `)` reads as division.
- Aliases are treated as external.
- Runtime indirection is out of reach.
- .mts, .cts and .jsx files are not scanned.
- A .d.ts-only target is unresolved.
- Paths over 500 characters throw.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Adds a new pure module, packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts, with its unit tests: the IO-free engine of CQ-V10.
- parseArchitectureRules validates a version-1 rules document. It refuses each malformed variant with INVALID_INPUT, naming the exact field.
- extractImports lexes JS/TS text. It returns every static, side-effect, re-export, type-only, literal import() and literal require() specifier with its 1-based line.
  - A non-literal import() or require() becomes an uncertainty and is never dropped.
  - Comments, string text, template text and regex bodies are never scanned as code.
- resolveImport maps a relative specifier onto tree paths: '.js' to .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs, and a directory to its index file. It returns null for external or unmatched specifiers.
- evaluateArchitecture selects only the rules whose from covers a changed path, and scans only the changed source files those rules cover.
  - It reports forbidden resolved imports as violations, and surfaces every uncertainty.
  - It applies failed > inconclusive > passed and sorts its output deterministically.
acceptanceCriteria: For the documented shape at its exact limits (100 rules, 32 prefixes, a 64-character id, a 300-unit reason), parseArchitectureRules returns a fresh canonical {version:1, rules}. It refuses each malformed variant with INVALID_INPUT and the exact context.field, one test per variant.

extractImports finds each documented import form with its line. It reports a non-literal import() as dynamic-import and a non-literal require() as non-literal-require. It ignores comments, strings, template text, regex bodies and member calls.

evaluateArchitecture selects rules only through whole-segment from coverage. It reports violations as {ruleId, file, line, specifier, resolved}, surfaces dynamic-import, non-literal-require and unresolved-relative uncertainty, applies failed > inconclusive > passed, and returns identical results for shuffled inputs.
In a fresh Linux snapshot, `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` and `npx tsc --noEmit` both exit 0.
invariants: The module imports only invalidInput from ../util/errors.js and normalizeAffectedFile from ../util/affectedFiles.js. It has no node: builtins, no IO and no module-level mutable state.
A non-literal import() or require() call is always surfaced as uncertainty. It is never dropped and never treated as external.
extractImports never throws on any string input; unterminated constructs end at EOF.
Outcome precedence: any violation gives failed, else any uncertainty gives inconclusive, else passed.
Ordering uses only code-unit comparison, never localeCompare, with a fixed object key order, so serialized output is identical across hosts and input orders.
A rule's forbid applies only to scanned files that its own from covers.
compatibility: No schema, store, tool, CLI or wire change; legacy behavior is untouched.
CQ-V10 (task-db328cda) consumes these exact names and the three uncertainty reasons. Do not rename them or add reasons.
approvedScope: Exports exactly as in the task description: ArchitectureRule, ArchitectureRules, parseArchitectureRules, ImportRef, ImportUncertainty, extractImports, resolveImport, ArchitectureFinding, ArchitectureResult and evaluateArchitecture. Nothing else is exported.
The lexer, the recognizer, the cooked-escape decoder, isRelative and covers are module-private.
Only the new delivery/architectureRules.ts and delivery/architectureRules.test.ts change.
reuse: invalidInput from packages/moe-daemon/src/util/errors.ts, for every refusal.

normalizeAffectedFile from packages/moe-daemon/src/util/affectedFiles.ts, plus the entry !== normalized idiom of validateCheckPaths in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/validators.ts, for both prefixes and changed paths.
The code-unit sort precedent of protectedPaths in packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.ts.
A new lexer is needed: no import scanner exists in the daemon sources, and typescript is only a devDependency in packages/moe-daemon/package.json.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-daemon/src/util/errors.ts: invalidInput(field, reason) returns a MoeError with code INVALID_INPUT, codeName 'INVALID_INPUT' and context {field, reason}.

packages/moe-daemon/src/util/affectedFiles.ts: normalizeAffectedFile(raw, fieldName) throws invalidInput(fieldName, ...) for a non-string, empty, absolute, drive-letter or '..' path. Otherwise it returns the path trimmed, with backslashes turned into '/', a leading './' stripped, and empty or '.' segments dropped.
packages/moe-daemon/tsconfig.json is strict, targets ES2022, and excludes src/**/*.test.ts from tsc.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. TypeScript compiler API (preProcessFile or a full AST). Rejected: typescript is only a devDependency, so it is not shipped at runtime, and the module may import only the two util modules.
2. Regexes over the raw text. Rejected: they cannot reliably skip comments, strings, templates and regex bodies, and they invite catastrophic backtracking.
3. A lexer dependency such as es-module-lexer or acorn. Rejected: a new runtime dependency, against the daemon's minimal dependency set and the import constraint.
4. CHOSEN: one linear hand-written lexer with JS line-terminator, cooked-escape and regex-context rules, plus a token-pattern recognizer. A clause scan bounded by the import/export keywords keeps it linear.
5. node:path posix in resolveImport. Excluded by the import constraint: a manual segment join takes a few lines and is platform-independent.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Field-path idiom: state/validators.ts validateRequiredChecks and validateCheckPaths use `${field}[${index}]` and `${itemField}.${key}` for unknown keys, and 'must be normalized: <n>' after normalizeAffectedFile.
- invalidInput(field, reason) gives code INVALID_INPUT, codeName 'INVALID_INPUT' and context {field, reason}. requiredChecks.test.ts asserts it with toMatchObject.
- Code-unit ordering precedent: protectedPaths in delivery/requiredChecks.ts ('deterministic across host locales').
- Consumer: step 2 of V10 (task-db328cda) builds `changed` {path, text} from diff-tree A/M/T paths and treePaths from ls-tree, and reads text only for .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs.
- tsconfig is strict with target ES2022. tsc excludes *.test.ts, so `tsc --noEmit` typechecks the module only; vitest does not typecheck.
planningNotes.risks:
- The regex-versus-division decision is a heuristic: in `if (x) /re/`, the regex after `)` reads as division. Line-local recovery bounds that to one line.
- JSX text in .tsx files, with apostrophes and slashes, is lexed as code; string and regex recovery keep the damage line-local.
- Every refusal must name the exact field, so tests must assert context.field, not just that something throws.
- The global rails reject the prototype-key token and the other forbidden tokens even in tests, so write no test for that key. Unknown-key refusal already covers any own key JSON.parse creates.
- The in-tree node_modules is Windows-native, so the gate runs in the Linux snapshot. HEAD carries peers' wip checkpoints: compare any red run with a baseline without the overlay, and never edit peer files.
- Keep the interface exactly as described; V10 is already planned against it. Keep the module around 350 lines.
